text:
maria gomez: Quick follow-up on the RFC — we need a clear approach for resume + idempotent apply when an air-gapped agent only received a subset of chunks. Do we want apply to be purely content-addressed and idempotent, or add an activation token exchange?

sahil rao: I still lean toward content-addressed idempotency. If each blob has a stable digest and we track applied digests + manifest version, re-applying is a no-op. Simpler for operators.

jen taylor: problem is partial manifests. If agent has blobs A,B but not C, and operator triggers apply with manifest referencing A,B,C — we need a deterministic failure vs a queued resume strategy. UX matters.

carol ng: we could add a lightweight install plan state machine on the agent: states = {fetching, validating, staged, activating}. If activation is requested and blobs missing -> return 409 + list of missing digests. Operator/console can then resume.

maria gomez: that sounds reasonable. How does that interact with signed bundles? We can't let an attacker flip manifests mid-download.

jen taylor: signed manifest with chain of signed chunk descriptors. Agent verifies signature before accepting blobs. For resume we keep a signed manifest fingerprint (sig_id) pinned to the install plan. Resume only allowed for that sig_id.

ops-bot: deploy 1736504321 started by @maria gomez — verification checks: manifest sig ok, agent has 0/3 blobs.

carol ng: Edge case: operator re-uploads a corrected blob C' with same filename but different digest. Since manifest is signed, agent will reject unless manifest updated. Good for safety.

dave li: Agree. Two tradeoffs: 1) Keep idempotent apply pure and let operator handle resume orchestration. 2) Make agents smarter with resume queues and retries. Option 2 increases agent complexity (storage accounting, long-lived state).

maria gomez: For on-prem customers we promised "minimal operator toil". That pushes us toward agents doing more, but keep the server-side simple. Any concrete API proposal?

sahil rao: API sketch: POST /install-plans {manifest_sig, desired_version}. Server returns plan_id. Agent polls GET /install-plans/:id -> {state, missing_digests:[...], pinned_sig}. Agent uploads blobs to local store via PUT /blobs/:digest. When missing_digests empty operator hits POST /install-plans/:id/activate. Activation will verify pinned_sig and move to staged.

jen taylor: Also add conditional-activate semantics: POST with header If-Match: <plan_etag> to avoid racey double-activates.

carol ng: For resume across network hiccups, implement chunked blob uploads with byte-range checks and a simple resumable session token per digest. Keep it optional; many customers will use rsync/offline USB.

maria gomez: OK. What about idempotency when applying the same manifest twice (retries)? We should log and return 200 if already active. If active but different content -> 409.

dave li: Implementation note: agent local DB should have table applied_manifests(manifest_sig TEXT PK, version TEXT, applied_at INT). Activation is an atomic rename from staging -> active dir. If rename fails, we roll back staging and keep applied_manifests unchanged.

jen taylor: We should also emit events for console: plan:created, plan:progress, plan:activated, plan:failed with structured missing list. That helps ops automation.

maria gomez: Good. Last question: do we support partial-apply (activate subset of components) or require all-or-nothing? My preference: all-or-nothing for safety, but support component-level manifests as future work.

carol ng: Agreed, start all-or-nothing. If customers want partial, they can craft multi-manifest plans.

maria gomez: Cool. Action items: Sahil to draft API RFC with plan lifecycle + error codes, Jen to add agent DB schema + atomic-activation pseudo-code, Carol to prototype resumable blob session. I'll wire up console event hooks. We'll reconvene in next architecture sync. :white_check_mark:
